findings.title: SSH Service Exposed on Port 22
remediation_commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade openssh-server
sudo nano /etc/ssh/sshd_config # Disable root login, use key-based auth
findings.description: SSH service is exposed on port 22 with OpenSSH 8.2p1. While this version is relatively recent, SSH services should be properly secured with key-based authentication and restricted access.
findings.recommendation: Implement key-based authentication, disable root login, and consider changing the default SSH port. Ensure strong passwords are used if password authentication is enabled.

findings.title: Outdated Apache HTTP Server on Port 80
remediation_commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade apache2
findings.description: Apache HTTP Server version 2.4.41 is running on port 80. This version has known vulnerabilities including Log4j-related issues and path traversal vulnerabilities. The server also exposes administrative directories.
findings.recommendation: Immediately update Apache to the latest version, implement security headers, and restrict access to administrative directories. Consider implementing a Web Application Firewall (WAF).

findings.title: Nginx with Weak SSL/TLS Configuration on Port 443
remediation_commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade nginx
findings.description: Nginx 1.18.0 is running on port 443 with HTTPS. The SSL/TLS configuration includes weak cipher suites (RC4, DES) and the SSL certificate is expiring soon. This version has known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Update Nginx to the latest version, reconfigure SSL/TLS to use only strong cipher suites, and renew the SSL certificate. Implement HSTS headers and disable weak protocols.

findings.title: MySQL Database Exposed on Port 3306

script_findings.output: Valid usernames found: root, mysql, admin

remediation_commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade mysql-server
sudo nano /etc/mysql/mysql.conf.d/mysqld.cnf # Bind to localhost only
findings.description: MySQL database server is exposed on port 3306 with version 8.0.25. Database services should never be exposed to external networks as they contain sensitive data and are frequent targets for attacks.
findings.recommendation: Immediately block external access to port 3306. Configure MySQL to bind only to localhost/127.0.0.1. Implement strong authentication, disable remote root login, and ensure all database users have strong passwords.

findings.title: PostgreSQL Database Exposed on Port 5432
remediation_commands: sudo -u postgres psql -c "ALTER USER postgres PASSWORD 'strong_password';"
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade postgresql
sudo nano /etc/postgresql/13/main/postgresql.conf # Bind to localhost only
findings.description: PostgreSQL database server is exposed on port 5432 with version 13.3. The default credentials (postgres:postgres) are still active, making this a critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately block external access to port 5432 and change all default passwords. Configure PostgreSQL to bind only to localhost. Implement proper authentication and access controls.

findings.title: Redis Cache Exposed on Port 6379
findings.banner: Redis server v=6.2.6 sha=00000000:0 malloc=jemalloc-5.1.0 bits=64

script_findings.output: INFO command accessible, CONFIG command accessible

remediation_commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade redis-server
findings.description: Redis cache server is exposed on port 6379 with version 6.2.6. Redis is running without authentication, allowing anyone to access and modify cached data. This is a critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately block external access to port 6379 and enable Redis authentication. Configure Redis to bind only to localhost. Implement proper access controls and monitoring.

summary: Comprehensive port scan completed with advanced service enumeration and vulnerability assessment
